commit.message:
fix(security): confine caller-supplied path args (arbitrary file read/write)

Same disclosure class reproduced on the grok-faf-mcp sibling (Zhihao Zhang,
WPI): caller `path` arguments flowed through path.resolve() into fs read/write
with no confinement (CWE-22/73/200), so absolute/`..` paths read or wrote files
outside the project (e.g. ~/.ssh/id_rsa, overwriting ~/.bashrc).

- New utils/safe-path.ts confinePath()/confineFileOp() chokepoint (ported from
  the grok fix): .faf tools may only read .faf/.fafm files; general file tools
  (faf_read/faf_write) confined to cwd + os.tmpdir() (override FAF_ALLOWED_ROOTS);
  symlink-canonical, blocks $HOME secrets, /etc, traversal, out-of-project writes.
- getProjectPath() now confines the explicit path; callTool() gains one central
  catch that converts PathConfinementError to a PATH DENIED result.
- fileHandler faf_read/faf_write route through confineFileOp; descriptions fixed.
- tests/security-path-confinement reproduces the PoC vectors (+ symlink bypass).

Full suite 359/359. Coordinated with the grok-faf-mcp advisory.

Assisted by Claude (Opus 4.8) · Approved by James Wolfe (@Wolfe-Jam)
